aspects.says: Close stands before SendResponse and TX keeps SendResponse from answering until the commit succeeded; a failed commit becomes a timeout and a reversal, and Close declared after SendResponse with TX set leaves every purchase unanswered.
basis: section:9.4 The Answer Waits for the Commit

aspects.says: A transaction holds its connection from Open to Close, paused ones too, so the pool is sized to the transactions that can be in between at once, with a connection-timeout under the terminal's.
basis: section:9.5 A Transaction Holds Its Connection From `Open` to `Close`

aspects.says: A transaction-log row is written on a connection of its own, from commit and abort of an abort participant after SendResponse, so a rollback doesn't erase the record of a decline.
basis: section:9.6 A Decline Is Recorded Outside the Transaction That Rolls It Back

aspects.says: A stored card number is found by an HMAC under a key kept outside the database; an unkeyed hash is reversed by hashing the few candidates that fit the known digits.
basis: section:9.7 A Stored Card Number Can Be Found Only With a Key

aspects.says: Open turns auto-commit off and leaves the connection in the Context, participants write through it, and Close commits or rolls back, so a decline anywhere in the chain undoes every write; a write through a connection of its own with auto-commit stays.
basis: section:9.2 One Database Transaction Spans the TransactionManager Transaction

aspects.says: The DataSource is a QBean that creates the pool, registers it in the NameRegistrar and closes it when Q2 stops, deployed before the TransactionManager.
basis: section:9.1 A Database Beside the Server
aspects.reason: it needs a pool library and a database server that the offline build does not include; the practices register their DataSource directly

aspects.says: The row lock taken in prepare lasts until Close, so a slow step between them makes every other transaction on that row wait for it.
basis: section:9.3 Write in `prepare`, So the Database Can Still Say No

aspects.says: A conditional UPDATE in prepare checks and reserves in one statement and holds the row lock until Close, so concurrent requests can't pass the same check and a database failure still becomes a decline; a check in prepare with the write in commit lets both through.
basis: section:9.3 Write in `prepare`, So the Database Can Still Say No
